items.context: Post-finalization validation results need to be persisted so the API can serve them. Two approaches: write a sibling JSON file (validation-report.json) alongside spec.json, or add a field directly to spec.json. The sibling file keeps spec.json clean and avoids schema changes, but adds a file to manage. Adding to spec.json is simpler to query but mixes concerns.

options.label: Sibling file (validation-report.json)
options.rationale: Clean separation of concerns. Validation results are ephemeral/regenerable data, not item metadata. Avoids spec.json schema changes. Can be deleted/regenerated independently. Recommended because it follows the same pattern as workshop rounds — structured data in its own file.

options.label: Field in spec.json
options.rationale: Single file to read for all item state. Simpler GET handler — no need to check for a separate file. But mixes regenerable validation data with authoritative item metadata.

items.context: When post-finalization validation fails, the item should not auto-queue. The system currently transitions items to 'ready' status after finalization. We need to decide how to prevent auto-queue while still allowing manual queue override.

options.label: Check validation-report.json in queue handler
options.rationale: The Queue handler (queue_ops.go) loads the validation report before queueing. If it exists and Passed=false, reject auto-queue but allow manual queue with a force flag. Keeps the logic in one place and doesn't require new status values.

options.label: New status value (e.g., 'ready_with_warnings')
options.rationale: Explicit status makes filtering easy and is visible in the data model. But adds a new lifecycle state that all code paths must handle, which is a larger change.

options.label: Marker file (.validation-failed)
options.rationale: Simple flag file checked during queue. Easy to implement but another file to manage alongside validation-report.json.

items.context: The 13 mandatory sections need to be detected in plan.md via header matching. Plans may use slightly different header formatting (e.g., '## Required Reading' vs '## 2. Required Reading' vs '## required-reading'). We need a matching strategy that's reliable without being brittle.

options.label: Normalized keyword matching
options.rationale: Lowercase the header, strip numbers/punctuation, then check if it contains key phrases like 'required reading', 'problem statement', etc. Simple, handles most formatting variations. Recommended for robustness without regex complexity.

options.label: Regex patterns per section
options.rationale: Write a regex for each section (e.g., `(?i)##\s*(?:\d+\.?\s*)?required\s+reading`). More precise but harder to maintain and debug. 13 regexes is a lot of patterns.

options.label: Exact string match with known variants
options.rationale: Maintain a list of known header strings per section. Simple but brittle — any new formatting variation requires a code change.

items.context: When gaps are found pre-finalization, they need to be appended to the finalize agent's prompt. The format should be clear enough for the agent to act on but concise enough not to bloat the prompt.

options.label: Structured markdown checklist
options.rationale:
Append a section like '## Plan Validation Gaps
- [ ] Missing: Testing Plan
- [ ] Missing: prompt-manager skill read command
...' — clear, actionable, agents parse markdown well. Recommended for clarity.

options.label: JSON block in prompt
options.rationale: Append the PlanValidationResult as a JSON code block. Precise and machine-readable, but agents handle markdown more naturally than embedded JSON.

items.text: The acceptance_allow and acceptance_deny patterns are already set on this item. acceptance_allow covers `scenarios/swarm-manager/api/internal/backlog/**`, `scenarios/swarm-manager/api/internal/workshop/**`, and `scenarios/swarm-manager/ui/src/**`. acceptance_deny protects `scenarios/swarm-manager/api/internal/execution/**`. These align well with the planned changes.

The `swarm-manager-workshop-finalize` skill defines the finalize agent's behavior. It reads plan.md, incorporates latest decisions, and writes a finalize round. The pre-finalization gap report would be appended to the prompt in `research.go` where the prompt is assembled (around the `fetchResearchPrompt` call), similar to how `req.Prompt` additional context is already appended.

This item is part of the 'swarm-manager-quality-gates' initiative alongside 'meta-orchestration-native-sessions' (idea) and 'initiative-level-oversight-design' (research). This validation gates item is the foundational piece — the other two items build on the assumption that finalized plans are structurally complete.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections populated. Defined 5-phase implementation strategy: core validation logic, pre-finalization gate, post-finalization gate, API surface, UI components. Identified key insertion points in research.go and workshop_save.go.
